plans.note: Primary text in Section 21 (Limitation of Liability); check the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Section 1 for the carve-out set and cross-check Section 20 indemnities are outside or super-capped. Test mutuality, cap multiple/measure (fees paid vs paid or payable) and exclusion of consequential loss.

Section 20 is the indemnification clause; confirm Vendor IP infringement and misconduct/data breach indemnities run to us, that defence/control and cost coverage exist, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow. Cross-reference Excluded Claims (Sec 1) and the cap in Section 21.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan Sections 2 (scope), 12 (Customer responsibilities), 26 (compliance) and 30 (General) for any restraint on our business or competing products before concluding absent. Absence is acceptable — no redline needed if nothing found.

Look for sole-source or 'all requirements' language in Section 2 (Agreement Structure and Scope), Section 4 (Order Forms/Affiliate Orders) and Section 12; likely absent, but exclusivity is sometimes buried in scope or pricing terms in Section 7.

Check Section 7 (Fees) and Section 4 for any best-pricing/most-favoured-customer language. Direction matters: an MFN in our favour is fine and must not be flagged; only a Customer-side obligation to give Vendor best terms is a deviation.
Non-solicits typically sit in General (Sec 30) or near confidentiality (Sec 16); if present, test duration, mutuality and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 (Termination) is primary; confirm Customer convenience right with reasonable notice and no early-termination penalty, and check Section 8 term structure plus Sections 7/10 for termination fees or unwind charges. Also confirm Vendor has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

Section 8 (Term and Renewal) governs auto-renewal and the non-renewal notice window; test notice length against playbook and check Section 7 for renewal price uplift. A missing uplift cap is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation.

Section 28 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution). Confirm the law is NY, DE, CA or England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seated arbitration; an accepted-but-not-preferred law is a rationale note only.

Section 24 (Assignment and Change of Control) is primary; confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor without consent, and that Vendor cannot terminate on our change of control. Check Section 30 for any residual general assignment language.

Section 14 (IP and Deliverables) for ownership of paid-for Deliverables and Section 15 (Customer Data) for data ownership; check Section 13 licence grants and the Deliverable/Vendor Technology/Customer Data definitions in Section 1 for any back-assignment or broad feedback/derived-data grab to Vendor.

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence) is primary; test scope for Affiliate and contractor use (cross-check Section 4 Affiliate Orders) and ensure the grant is not revocable at will or unilaterally suspendable outside a payment/breach trigger.

Section 22 (Audit Rights) — check frequency limits, advance written notice, business-hours/off-site preference and who bears cost. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may hold record-retention and our reciprocal assurance rights; do not flag rights running in our favour.

Look for late-payment penalties or liquidated sums payable by us in Section 7, and any SLA/service-credit mechanics in Section 3. Service credits payable to us are beneficial and must not be flagged; only Customer-payable liquidated damages are a deviation. Avoid double-flagging early-termination fees already covered under T4C.

Section 19 (Warranties) is primary — test warranty period, professional/conforming-services standard, and whether the remedy is real (re-performance plus refund) rather than sole-and-exclusive re-performance only. Cross-check Section 6 acceptance and Section 3 performance standards.
Section 18 (Insurance) exists; verify coverage lines and limits (general liability, professional/E&O, cyber given Vendor hosts Customer Data per Sections 15/17) and evidence-of-cover obligations.

Check Section 7 (Fees) and Section 4 (Order Forms) for committed spend, minimum volumes or non-reducible seat counts, and Section 8 for commitments carried into renewal terms. If a commitment exists, confirm an exit path exists before flagging.

Section 11 (Transition Assistance and Data Return) is on point; confirm minimum assistance period, export format and timing for Customer Data return, and that assistance is not conditioned on our being non-breaching or on unbounded extra fees. Cross-check Section 10 effects of termination and Section 15 data deletion obligations.
